_meta.description: Named sandbox configurations to measure. Every preset shipped here was executed on a Linux host on 2026-09-08 and produced a probe result; none is transcribed from documentation. Presets named after a third-party agent's sandbox must cite that agent's source in `source` and are not shipped until its code has been read.
_meta.schema: kind=container needs engine+flags; kind=command needs template containing {probe}

bwrap-ro-root.rationale: A common lightweight pattern: the whole host filesystem read-only, own PID namespace, network still shared. Shows what read-only alone does and does not buy. No named agent is claimed to use this; it is a configuration, not a citation.

bwrap-unshare-all.rationale: The same, with every namespace unshared, so the network is gone. The environment is still inherited from the parent.

bwrap-unshare-all-clearenv.rationale: Adds --clearenv. Compare against bwrap-unshare-all to see exactly what the parent's environment was handing the agent.

bwrap-workdir-net.rationale: System directories read-only, one writable working directory, network left on so the agent can fetch packages. A plausible coding-agent sandbox shape, composed here rather than taken from any named product.
bwrap-workdir-net.source: composed to represent the common pattern; verified 2026-09-08

codex-cli-0.153.4-bwrap-layer.rationale: The bubblewrap layer of OpenAI Codex CLI 0.153.4 --sandbox read-only, copied verbatim from the live process argv (see source). It reproduces ONE of the two layers. Codex then execs its own helper with --apply-seccomp-then-exec and a --permission-profile, and that second layer is what refuses unix-domain bind and connect. Running this preset therefore scores HIGHER than the real sandbox, and the difference is the seccomp filter. Use it to see what bubblewrap alone buys, not as a stand-in for Codex.
codex-cli-0.153.4-bwrap-layer.source: captured from /proc/<pid>/cmdline of the live bwrap process during a codex exec run, 2026-09-09, Codex CLI 0.153.4 on Ubuntu 24.04. The --argv0 and the vendor binary path that followed are omitted because they are host-specific and not part of the confinement. Corroborated by the vendor's own documentation at https://learn.chatgpt.com/codex/sandboxing (fetched 2026-09-08), which states the Linux sandbox relies on bubblewrap for enforcement; the argv itself is first-hand, not taken from that page.

docker-default.rationale: A container run the way most quick-start docs show it: root inside, full network, writable root filesystem, default capability set.

docker-hardened.rationale: Every control at once: no network, immutable root, no capabilities, unprivileged user, resource limits. The reference point a real agent sandbox should be measured against.
docker-hardened.source: composed from docker run options; verified 2026-09-08

docker-no-network.rationale: The single cheapest control: an agent that cannot open a socket cannot exfiltrate, whatever it is talked into doing.

docker-readonly.rationale: Immutable root filesystem with scratch space, so a compromised agent cannot persist changes into the image layer.

podman-rootless-default.rationale: Rootless podman with default flags: the container's root is a namespaced root mapped to an unprivileged host uid, which changes what 'runs as root' costs.

podman-rootless-hardened.rationale: The hardened flag set under rootless podman, for teams that cannot give the agent a docker socket at all.
